answers.question: What was the task?
answers.answer: To rename the server timeout setting so that its name shows milliseconds.
quotes: The task was to rename the server timeout setting so that its name shows milliseconds.

answers.question: How did it end: what is done and what is not?
answers.answer: The rename is done in the code and in our settings file and both tests pass, but the operations team's production file still uses the old name.
quotes: That is done in the code and in our settings file, and both tests pass.
The operations team's production file still sets the timeout under the old name.

answers.question: How does the thing that changed work?
answers.answer: The code reads only the new name, falls back to five seconds when it is missing, and our settings file gives three seconds under the new name.
quotes: The code now reads only the new name.
When the name is missing, it falls back to five seconds.
Our settings file gives three seconds under the new name.

answers.question: What is the problem, and what causes it?
answers.answer: The production file still sets the timeout under the old name, which the code no longer reads, so production waits three seconds instead of ten.
quotes: The operations team's production file still sets the timeout under the old name.
The code no longer reads that name, so after the release production waits three seconds instead of ten.

answers.question: What is not verified?
answers.answer: The tests do not read the production file, so production's behaviour is not checked by them.
quotes: The tests check both cases. They do not read the production file.

answers.question: What do I have to decide, and what does each option give and cost?
answers.answer: Whether operations rename their line before the release (one name everywhere, but the release waits) or the code also reads the old name (release can go now and production keeps ten seconds, but two names live in the code until operations rename and the old one is removed).
quotes: You decide whether operations rename their line first, or the code keeps reading the old name for a while.
Operations rename their line to the new name before the release
one name everywhere, nothing to clean up later
the release waits for the operations team
The code also reads the old name, and the old name wins while it is set
the release can go now, and production keeps ten seconds
two names live in the code until operations rename their line and I remove the old one
